title: The Buzzer
subtitle: UVB-76 · Russia, 1970s–
voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.
grade: Desaturated documentary still, a remote Russian military shortwave radio transmitter station in a snowy birch and pine forest, rusted steel antenna towers disappearing into low cloud, an old concrete blockhouse with rusted iron door, dim fluorescent interior with vintage 1970s-80s Soviet radio equipment, paper logs, and a single microphone, melancholy and uncanny, period 1970s-to-present detail, cinematic wide composition, fine film grain, no text, no signage, no people, no faces.

beats.vo: Somewhere in a forest south of Moscow, a radio tower has broadcast the same tone, on the same frequency, for more than forty years.
beats.img: A tall rusted steel radio transmission tower in a remote snowy Russian birch and pine forest under heavy overcast, distant concrete blockhouse, eerie and isolated, no people.

beats.vo: A short buzz. Twenty-five times a minute. Day and night.
beats.img: An old Soviet-era radio room interior with dim fluorescent light, a single microphone on a steel desk, vintage meters and indicator lamps, paper logbook, eerie, no people.

beats.vo: Occasionally, the buzz stops. A voice reads Russian names and numbers, for a few minutes. Then the buzz returns.
beats.cap:

then the buzz returns
beats.img: A close-up of an old Soviet mechanical typewriter with a sheet of paper bearing Cyrillic text, dim desk-lamp light, vintage shortwave log, documentary still, no readable text, no people.

beats.vo: The Russian government has never explained its purpose.

beats.img: A vast empty Russian winter forest under low grey overcast with a distant rusted radio tower, deep snow, cold fading light at dusk, melancholy and unresolved, no people.
